system: Session Inbox delivery, admission, submission and continuation scheduling

bounds.delivery: Two concurrent clients each publish one immutable input ID. Body, RPC offer, user receipt and activation reach one authorized execution host in arbitrary order. Latest activation has a fixed LWW winner (ID 2); reversing both IDs is symmetric. Each arrival is represented once; duplicate packet idempotence is an abstraction, not a network implementation proof. At most two missing-history timeouts; no host migration of storage.
bounds.sqlite: All 336 orders of accept A < begin A < submit A < settle A < release A, interleaved with accept B, exact-target Stop, lease-safe epoch change. SQL transactions are real; the provider-start critical section is represented by consecutive synchronous canSubmit/fence. One preexisting result and one future result. Future new-ID input is admitted after each timeline.
bounds.outputGate: One RPC turn with waiting/opening/open phases, original deadline retained during callback, disposal, callback completion/hang, output, abort and stale-write attempt. Signal guard prevents late writes; raw already-issued work is not modeled as canceled. No global Wait. Metadata creation remains eligible after timeout while the turn is live.

assumptions: Execution host handoff occurs only after the prior physical host lease/process-exit barrier. This barrier is assumed, not produced by tests.

Fair delivery profiles assume enabled arrival and local processing steps eventually run. Permanent partition profile intentionally disables both payload sources for input 1; it checks input 2 progress, not impossible input 1 execution.
Receipt presence is not cryptographic authorization; execution still requires existing verified signer, principal, access and durable admission. These are outside this model and never bypassed.
Delivery and output are separate slices of the same system, not a proved full composition/refinement of the watcher, SQL, provider and frontend.

These slices describe an active workspace; daemon identity-restoration sealing/restart and cache GC remain outside the modeled lifecycle. The merged production changes retain the existing delivery selection, receipts and Stop/start fences.
limits: Finite slices, not a proof of full implementation composition. No actual Loro/Roost replication/reconnect, E2EE/revocation, host-lease producer, real provider, OS disk exhaustion or UI/device acceptance. Declarations and recovery/RPC-selection methods are compiled unchanged with actual policy helpers and synthetic document ports. The complete assistant-entry writer is also compiled unchanged; its tested existing-author branch uses a synthetic SQLite history port and a diagnostic span stub. This is a cancellation-fence witness, not full HistoryWriter acceptance. Host epochs assume an already-safe handoff. Per-ID receipts grow with failed identities; only the serialized host appends them. The default checks current finite temporal properties; source-only and safety-only cannot replace that result. Full workspace checks require dependencies absent from this nested checkout.

properties.ReceiptBeforeStart: Receipt and usable payload precede modeled admission/start; does not validate signatures.
properties.PayloadBeforeStart: Either synchronized history or full RPC payload is present.
properties.NoFailedReplay: An input already surfaced as not delivered must not become an execution candidate when another timeout replaces the scalar marker. Source witness stops at candidate selection.
properties.EveryInputOutcome: Under eventual delivery and fair local steps, each of the two inputs reaches completion or explicit missing-history failure.
properties.HealthySecondProgress: Even if input 1 payload never arrives, input 2 eventually completes or gets an explicit delivery failure.
properties.DisposeUnblocks: Disposing an old RPC output gate eventually releases its already-waiting writers.
properties.OutputEventuallyUnblocked: Under the configured callback/disposal fairness, output gate waiters eventually release.
properties.NoLateWrites: Only disposal aborts later assistant-entry writes, including disposal after deadline already released waiters. Already-issued work is not canceled.
properties.DeadlineUnblocks: The original deadline releases output even if the pre-open callback remains pending; no disposal fairness is assumed.
properties.LiveCallbackKeepsMetadata: A completing callback on a still-live turn retains author/model metadata after the wait deadline.

actions.Body/Rpc/Receipt/Activation: session-send-delivery.ts separate history/control/meta writes and dispatch-turn RPC; delivery order is abstracted, not real transport.
actions.Expire: markMissingUserTurnRecovery records the exact failed ID in missingHistoryUserMsgIds with the legacy scalar; source replay also rejects an old timeout after activation changes.
actions.Accept/Start/Finish: watcher source selection plus session-execution-service acceptInboxHumanInput and durable Inbox admission; start/retirement are abstract boundary conditions checked separately by real SQL permutations.
actions.ObserveHistory/Deadline: turn-history-gate.ts scheduleCheck/openGate synchronous prefix through hook await.
actions.HookCompletes: Callback resolution/caught rejection releases only its own gate; the writer checks its abort signal after asynchronous reads and before openAssistantTurn.
actions.Dispose: Aborts later callback steps even on an already-open gate, then releases waiters. Deadline only releases waiters.
actions.sqlitePermutations: InboxSqlite accept, begin, prepare, canSubmit, fence, settle, release, pause and activate; no handwritten SQL implementation of those transitions.
